label: Long Voyage test: the phone game on the board, BLE sync (game firmware 0.2.0)
notes: Test build for the bench, not a stable release; nothing updates to it on its own. Needs game firmware lv-core 0.2.0 first: flash lv-core-0.2.0-2661c2144844-RPI_PICO_W.uf2 by hand (hold BOOTSEL, drop the file on the RPI-RP2 drive); this page refuses to install on any other firmware (boards on lv-core 0.1.0 install 0.1.0-lv-test). Then set the ship number in section 4, the crew codes and the launch date (flight day 1 starts at 06:00 that day and a new flight day every morning at 06:00, 42 days; leave it blank for the manual bench day), install, and power-cycle. Join the LV-<ship number> hotspot with a phone: the game opens by itself (or browse to any http address) and every crew member signs in with their code. BLE sync between ships keeps running. New in this build: lv-core 0.2.0 has the whole game frozen into the firmware (the game core, the board modules and the story pack), so the board runs it from flash instead of loading it into memory: about 28 KB more free heap while two phones play during a BLE sync, and a much smaller install (main.py, the phone page and engage.bin). Installing removes the copies a 0.1.0 install left on the board. Same game as 0.1.0-lv-test otherwise: the phone talks to you in the second person, the first-run briefing, Bluetooth range in the crew list and gift pickers, the optional ship battery (game/docs/BATTERY.md) and the breathing ship light. Faster bench: from the repo, python3 game/tools/bench.py --ship N installs this build over USB, runs the self-test and prints a PASS/FAIL report (docs/BENCH_TEST.md). Check from the REPL with: import selftest; selftest.run(120). Your settings in data/ are kept. To go back, flash lv-core 0.1.0 and install 0.1.0-lv-test. Sealed board: main.py waits 2 s after power-up before touching the radio, so any mpremote command (Ctrl-C) in that window gets the REPL; an empty data/safe skips the game on every boot.
